Medicaid waste isn't theoretical—it's crushing taxpayers. $934B budget, yet fraud investigations exposed billions vanishing into administrative black holes and inflated pharma contracts. Not a penny reached patients.

Look at the data: Hospital executive compensation up 78% while rural clinics close. Big Pharma charging 312% markup on basic medications. Veterans waiting months for basic care.

The solution isn't throwing more money at broken systems. Real reform means blockchain tracking of every federal dollar, competitive bidding on all contracts, and criminal penalties for administrators who sign off on waste.

Cutting bureaucratic bloat isn't cruel—it's essential. When government burns cash on admin overhead, it's vulnerable Americans who pay the price. Every dollar wasted is care denied.

Accountability isn't optional. It's the difference between helping people and funding failure.
